security_audit.summary: Review found one medium-risk temporary-file pattern and no malicious or deceptive intent. The predictable /tmp issue body can be replaced or symlinked before GitHub CLI reads it. Remaining alerts are Markdown backticks, fixed argument-list subprocess calls, validation output, or intentional GitHub metadata queries.

remediation.issue: The creation example uses the predictable shared path /tmp/issue-body.md.
remediation.suggestion: Create the body with a secure temporary-file utility, restrict permissions, pass its generated path to GitHub CLI, and delete it afterward.

content.value_statement: Poorly structured issues create ambiguity and require manual cleanup. This skill drafts and validates titles, bodies, labels, milestones, projects, and relationships.
actual_capabilities: Validates issue titles for imperative wording, length, vague phrasing, punctuation, and redundant type prefixes.
Drafts standard, bug, and feature issue bodies with acceptance criteria and relevant context sections.
Recommends type, priority, scope, branch, milestone, and project metadata from repository context.
Lists GitHub labels, milestones, and user projects through authenticated GitHub CLI commands.
Creates GitHub issues and guides project placement, parent-child links, blockers, and related issue references.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI installation and authentication for repository queries or issue creation.
Applies the included conventions, which may differ from an established repository taxonomy.
Scope detection depends on local configuration, branch names, or detectable project structure.
Project and relationship updates may require additional permissions or companion skills.

use_cases.title: Document a Reproducible Bug
use_cases.description: Turn a bug report into a complete issue with reproduction steps, expected behavior, acceptance criteria, and labels.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Work
use_cases.description: Validate titles and select consistent type, priority, and scope labels for incoming work.

use_cases.title: Plan a Release
use_cases.description: Prepare related issues with milestones, project placement, dependencies, and parent-child structure.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Issue Title
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this issue title: "[BUG] Login fails". Suggest an imperative title without a type prefix and explain the change.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Bug Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a bug issue for {problem}. Include reproduction steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, acceptance criteria, environment details, and recommended labels.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Feature Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a feature issue plan for {capability}. Propose the title, body, type, priority, scope, milestone, and project placement. Ask before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Issue Hierarchy
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {work_items} and design a parent-child issue structure. Identify blockers and related work, then prepare complete issue content and GitHub metadata.

output_examples.input: Review the title: [FEATURE] Add dark mode
output: Suggested title: Add dark mode support
Scope: confirm the affected interface component before creation

output_examples.input: Draft an issue for login failures with special characters.
output: Summary: Fix authentication failures for passwords containing supported special characters.
Acceptance criteria cover successful login, specific validation errors, regression tests, and unchanged standard login behavior.
Recommended labels: bug, priority:high, and the repository authentication scope.

output_examples.input: Plan issues for a new authentication system.
output: Create one parent feature issue describing the authentication outcome and shared constraints.
Create child issues for storage, API endpoints, interface changes, tests, and documentation.
Confirm project, milestone, priorities, scopes, and blockers before creating any issue.

best_practices: Confirm scope, priority, milestone, project placement, and relationships before creating external issues.
Use one primary type label, one priority label, and at least one specific scope label.
Verify created issues, project items, and relationships immediately after each external update.
anti_patterns: Do not place type prefixes in titles when labels already express the issue type.
Do not create issues with vague summaries or acceptance criteria that cannot be tested.
Do not use task lists as a substitute for GitHub parent-child relationships.

faq.question: Can this skill create GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses authenticated GitHub CLI commands when creation is requested and required metadata is available.

faq.question: Does it require repository configuration?
faq.answer: No. It can draft content without configuration, but scope and project suggestions improve when repository context is available.

faq.question: Can it validate existing issue titles?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks length, imperative wording, vague phrases, ending punctuation, and redundant type prefixes.

faq.question: When does it use network access?
faq.answer: Only GitHub queries and updates require network access. Local title validation and drafting do not.

faq.question: Can it manage issue relationships?
faq.answer: It documents blockers and related issues. True sub-issue links may require the companion relationship workflow and suitable GitHub permissions.

faq.question: Can I use custom labels?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the repository taxonomy or available labels because the bundled defaults may not match every project.
